newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares chalk up gains after narrow trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares chalk up gains after narrow trade.

text.p: Greek equities traded in positive territory on Thursday settling with gains of 0.5 percent. Banks and industrials moved higher but construction shares showed weakness and fell 1.59 percent.

"The market has not valued the construction sector's potential in 1997 and beyond. Buying interest keeps chasing banks and is slowly shifting into industrials but not yet in the construction sector," said analyst Nick Galousis at Kappa Securities.
Market watchers expected narrow trade in the next few days.

Following a better-than-expected March CPI inflation figure -- 6.0 percent -- banks started a new round of interest rate cuts last week. The focus now is on April CPI which is expected to dip below 6.0 percent.
An informal Reuters poll of bankers and economists produced a mean forecast of 5.7 percent. Forecasts ranged from 5.5 - 6.0 percent.
Subscriptions to Xiosbank's IPO started on Tuesday April 15 and end Friday April 18. The bank is going public at 2,650 drachmas a share seeking to raise 4.43 billion.
The Athens general share index ended 0.50 percent or 7.09 points higher at 1,420.51 from Wednesday's 1,413.42 close, after opening at 1,418.70. The session's high was at 1,424.03.
Turnover was 12.4 billion drachmas on volume of 4.3 million shares. Decliners led advancers 118 to 106 with 17 issues unchanged on 241 traded.
Banks gained 0.68 percent with construction falling 1.59 percent. Industrials strengthened 0.74 percent.
